decisions.rationale: Names the single specific disease Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy with its X-linked qualifier, which is part of the most specific form of the name, so the whole phrase is kept.
Full name of one specific disease (Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy) that is defined without further subcategorization; it is a separate mention in the second sentence and duplicates are annotated.
Abbreviation EDMD is a synonymous mention of Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy and is annotated as its own separate mention.
X-linked recessive muscular dystrophy describes a family of multiple specific muscular dystrophies rather than one defined disease, analogous to the autosomal recessive disease example.
Muscle wasting is a clinical sign or symptom describing a finding rather than a disease name or disease family, so it is not annotated.
Cardiomyopathy refers to a family of multiple specific diseases of the heart muscle, so it is a Disease Class mention.
Cardiac conduction defects refers to a group of distinct conduction disorders rather than a generic term like abnormalities, so it is treated as a grey-area Disease Class mention.
EDMD in patients with EDMD is used as the head disease name of the patient group and is not functioning as a modifier, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
EDMD in unrelated EDMD patients modifies the noun patients, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
EDMD in usual EDMD phenotype modifies the noun phenotype, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
EDMD in the clinical features of EDMD refers to the disease itself as the object of the phrase and does not modify another noun, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
